hints: Focus on the first step of electrophilic addition, where H+ from HBr adds to the C=C bond to make a carbocation.
Adding H+ to the two different ends of the double bond in $(CH_3)_2C=CHCH_3$ gives one tertiary and one secondary carbocation.
Recall that more alkyl groups stabilise a positive charge better, so pick the structure with the positive carbon joined to three other carbons and with no Br attached yet.
walkthrough:
**Draw the starting alkene**

Think of 2-methylbut-2-ene simply as an unsymmetrical double bond. Its structure is:
$$ (CH_3)_2C=CHCH_3 $$
The left carbon has two methyl groups, the right carbon has one H and one methyl group.

**Make the two possible carbocations**

H+ from HBr can add to either end of the C=C bond, and the positive charge goes on the other carbon.
$$ (CH_3)_2C=CHCH_3 + H^+ \rightarrow carbocation $$
If H+ adds to the right carbon, you get $(CH_3)_2C^+-CH_2CH_3$, a tertiary carbocation. If H+ adds to the left carbon, you get $(CH_3)_2CH-C^+(H)CH_3$, a secondary carbocation.

**Choose the more stable intermediate**

Carbocation stability increases with more electron-donating alkyl groups around the positive carbon: tertiary > secondary > primary.
$$ tertiary \; (3 \; alkyl \; groups) > secondary \; (2 \; alkyl \; groups) $$
So the more stable intermediate is the tertiary cation with the + on the carbon joined to two $CH_3$ groups and one $CH_2CH_3$ group, and no Br present yet.

options.A: Shows $(CH_3)_2C^+-CH_2CH_3$, the tertiary carbocation. The positive carbon is bonded to three alkyl groups, so it gets maximum inductive electron donation and hyperconjugation. This is the more stable intermediate and leads to the major Markovnikov product.
options.B: Shows $(CH_3)_2CH-C^+(H)CH_3$, the secondary carbocation. It has only two alkyl groups on the positive carbon, so it is less stabilised than the tertiary cation. Students who forget to count alkyl groups often pick this.
options.C: Shows a structure already containing Br with a positive charge. In electrophilic addition, Br- adds after the carbocation is formed, so Br is not present in the carbocation intermediate. This confuses the intermediate with the final product step.
options.D: Shows another structure already containing Br with a positive charge. Like C, this cannot be the H+ addition intermediate because the C-Br bond has not formed yet at that stage. It also places the charge incorrectly.
